title: Resolve imprecise voice terminology using repository evidence

source.fixture_note: Uses the same historical Patchbay Go README captured for case 001, later in the same demo. This session read source code; replay tests README grounding only.

input.transcript: How do we block the dangerous commands from being resolved?

observed.reply: The blocking happens in the raw route in the worker file. When someone hits the raw path, the worker decodes the base64-encoded URI, then runs it through a function called isSafeScheme, which extracts the scheme prefix and looks it up in a blocklist of browser-privileged schemes like javascript, data, http, https, file, and about. If the scheme is on that list, or if there's no clean scheme at all, the worker refuses with a 400 error and fails closed, so only true native app schemes ever get redirected.
observed.note: Illustrates correct referent resolution; not an independently scored historical pass.

expected.reference_answer: The raw route checks URI schemes and refuses browser-privileged ones with HTTP 400, so wrapped links can open native apps without becoming script-execution links or open redirects.
